items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: I worked with Al Schmidt a couple of times with Tommy LiPuma

ctx.x: Do you have an opinion, with all the recording you’ve done, someone comes out and they’ve got, you know ten or twelve microphones on the drum set. Is it overkill? Does it affect the way you play because you kind of know that the reason they have all these microphones is they’re going to fuss around with the balance?

I understand the engineer’s perspective, he wants to have choices — bottom of the snare drum, top of the snare drum, each tom-tom, overhead cymbals. A lot of guys these days want to have the sound from the drummer’s perspective so they balance things left and right so when you listen back to it if you’re a right handed drummer you’re hearing the hi-hat on the right side and the ride cymbal on the left side. Which is fine you know. But I think ten or twelve microphones is overkill as far as I’m concerned. If you…
I had a moment in the studio once, I wonder if you had a moment like this. The first time I saw tape sliced with a razor blade and hooked back together I said what is that? This actually works?
